description.narrative:
The project contributes to and is aligned to the UN Women “Advancing Women’s Leadership, Empowerment and Resilience in Uganda’s Refugee Response: Phase II” and directly contributes to Outcome 3. The project intends to achieve the following results:
Goal: Positive coping mechanisms and sustainable economic activities are promoted for refugee and host community women and girls.
Outcome 1.0: Refugee and host community women have increased access to sustainable non-agricultural livelihood opportunities.
Output 1.1: Establishment and roll out of savings and lending groups to (105) 3,150 women including digitalisation of savings and linkages to financial institutions such as banks. (10 percent PWDs) -Implemented by OXFAM and URDMC
The 105 women's groups, each with 30 members, engaged in income-generating activities of the Village Savings and Loan Association methodology through engagement with the ENSIBUUKO company for digital VSLA. This will help in the profiling of VSLA and Framers groups, financial linkages, a digital marketplace for farmers, and e-learning through an Android-based smart phone application. These groups will also receive support in the form of tabs or smartphones to aid their saving and financial literacy training and groupdynamics training. Oxfam and its partners will work with the district commercial officer, district community development officer, and office of the prime minister to monitor the groups,minimise related risk, and ensure sustainability once they are matureand have been saving for at least a year.
Output 1.2: Support75 women groups comprising of 2,250 women and youth to establish and manage small and enterprises, support with business and financial skills training including capitalization of businessesand linkages to value addition chains for refugee women through increasingproduction, and support to establish cottage industries and linkages to market opportunities. Implemented by OXFAM

participating-org.narrative:
Uganda Refugee and Disaster Management Council (URDMC) is a registered Ugandan-based Non-Governmental Organization registration No: S.5914/9502 with its Headquarter in Gulu and Field Office located on Gulu-Adjumani Road, adjacent to Pakele Police Post, Pakele Town Board. The organization was founded in 2012 with aims of protection of refugee#s rights through Food Distribution and Ware house management. URDMC partnered with MOBAN in collaboration with GIZ International in the implementation of Peace building project within Nakivale Refugees# Settlement-Western Uganda in 2012/2013. URDMC in close collaboration with OPM in South Western Uganda also contributed towards the emergency response for the Congolese Refugees in Matanda Transit Centre. In partnership with Apparel Art Uganda,URDMC is supporting child mothers in Northern Uganda with the aim of economically empowering them to exercise their rights and meettheir basic needs through creative arts and designs.
The Vision is: To be the leading organization in the protection of refugees#right and people affected by conflict and disaster# and the Mission is : #To promote and protect the rights of people who havebeen forced to flee their countries or their home regardless of their race, religion, nationality or political affiliations#.
The organisation has over three (3) years# experience in working with the people affected by disaster and conflict, especially the vulnerable children, youth and women to rebuild their lives and to promote peaceful co-existence and sustainable livelihoods in the community. URDMC believes that all people are equal and have the right to determine and direct their development, and to live in dignity regardless of background, status, and tribe, political and religious affiliation
